summary:
Allwork.Space reports that U.S. office demand is strengthening while supply shrinks, pushing up rents for premium space. The third quarter of 2026 marked the fifth consecutive quarter of positive net absorption, with occupiers taking a net 6 million square feet, and new leases averaging a 13% larger tenant footprint, per CNBC.

Supply is tightening on both ends. Only 3.5 million square feet of new office space was delivered in Q3 2026, matching the near-record low of Q2, while 9.6 million square feet was removed through conversions and redevelopment. National office inventory has fallen by 45 million square feet since the end of 2023, and just 23 million square feet is currently under construction.

That scarcity is lifting rents at the top of the market. Effective rents for first-generation trophy space rose more than 20% year over year in Q3 2026. Second-generation trophy space rents rose 10% as tenants shifted to existing premium buildings when newer options became scarce.

Geographically, technology companies are driving net absorption in San Francisco and Austin. Leasing volume in Sun Belt gateway markets rose 13% year over year, and smaller tertiary markets recovered to roughly 95% of their 2019 leasing volume.

Construction remains constrained despite improving fundamentals. Willy Walker, CEO of commercial real estate finance and advisory firm Walker & Dunlop, said office construction this year is running at about 9% of normal annual supply and attributed the shortfall to limited equity capital. The article concludes that the development pipeline is small relative to a market where demand is improving and existing stock is being withdrawn.

The piece is market-level commercial real estate reporting. It does not address workplace operations topics such as desk booking, visitor management, attendance tracking, or hybrid policy mechanics.
